# Accounting Analytics: An Integrated Approach {#accounting-analytics-a-practical-approach .unnumbered}

This open educational resource textbook teaches accounting students to extract, prepare, analyze, and visualize financial and operational data using Microsoft Excel, SQL, and Microsoft Power BI, three tools widely adopted in professional practice. Every technique is taught through accounting questions, and every example draws on the data of a single company, so students see how analytics supports financial reporting, management decisions, and audit work.

The book is designed for undergraduate and graduate accounting and business students with no prior analytics or programming experience. Introductory financial and managerial accounting provides the foundation. Applied exercises in every chapter look at each technique from the perspectives of financial accounting, managerial accounting, and auditing. Throughout the book, the Charles River Accounting Dataset provides a common setting for learning across all three tools.


## What This Book Covers {.unnumbered}

The chapters of the book are organized into five parts. Part I establishes the conceptual foundations of accounting analytics, including data types, data quality, and the relational database model, and closes with a case that prepares the company's data for analysis. Part II teaches data preparation, descriptive analytics, statistical modeling, and audit testing in Microsoft Excel. Part III introduces SQL for querying relational databases, joining tables, performing aggregations, and conducting population-level audit analytics. Part IV covers data visualization principles and interactive dashboard design in Microsoft Power BI. Part V integrates all three tools in applied projects spanning financial reporting analytics, cost and management accounting, forensic accounting, and emerging technologies.

The book is under development. Chapters are published as they are completed, and the [Downloads](#sec-downloads) page always provides the latest version of the book.


## Where to Start {.unnumbered}

- **Instructors** can begin with the [Preface](#sec-preface), which describes the pedagogical design, the intended audience, and how the book is organized.
- **Students** can begin with [To the Student](#sec-to-the-student), which explains what to expect from each chapter and how to succeed with the material.
- **Every reader** can meet the company behind the data in [About the Dataset](#sec-about-the-dataset) and find the book and dataset files on the [Downloads](#sec-downloads) page.


## Open Access {.unnumbered}

This textbook is an open educational resource distributed at no cost, and all software tools used in the exercises are free or included with standard institutional licenses. No student should be prevented from developing analytics skills because of software cost or platform limitations.

Unless otherwise noted, this work is licensed under [Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 International (CC BY-SA 4.0)](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/). You may share and adapt the material, including for commercial use, provided you give appropriate credit, link to the license, indicate any changes, and distribute adaptations under the same license. Do not add restrictions that limit the permissions the license provides.


## Contributing {.unnumbered}

This book is a living project, and contributions from instructors, students, and practitioners are welcome. To report an error in the text, examples, datasets, or links, or to suggest an improvement, open an issue on the [GitHub Issues page](https://github.com/mmcodesso/Accounting_Analytics_Book/issues). To propose a change directly, submit a pull request on the book's [GitHub repository](https://github.com/mmcodesso/Accounting_Analytics_Book). Instructors who use the book in their courses are invited to share their experience and adapted materials through the repository. The open educational resource model works best when the community around the resource is active.
